text:
incident-bot: ALERT: customer=Hanover Corp (vpc: eu-west-1) observed spike of 429s from dedicated pool hanover-prod-1. 429 rate ~18% over last 5m, errors rising. Pager: on-call-eng-sre. Tags: #priority-high :rotating_light:
ops-bot: automatic mitigation tried: throttling bypass attempted, diverted 12% traffic to fallback model (gptx-small-v2) — success rate ~60% for requests; still seeing backpressure on hanover-prod-1.
alex: oncall here, seeing the same. Routing logs show prefix cache miss spike and a burst of long-context requests (seq len > 4096).
priya: @alex any immediate customer-facing action we can take? do we have permission to grant burst?
alex: not yet. Need approval from account + infra. tagging @account-anna for contract override.
account-anna: pinged hanover CSM, they confirm we can do a temporary emergency override for up to 6 hours. Need an ops approval and SRE manual lift.
jamie: I can make the pool-level rate limit exception in the control plane. steps: 1) create temp policy, 2) increase pool qps by 3x, 3) set auto-revert at T+6h. Anyone object?
maria: question: will increasing qps exhaust shared capacity? hanover-prod-1 is dedicated but uses burst borrowing for short windows — check cross-customer impact.
alex: good catch. I ran capacity check — spare headroom 40% on that shard, but two other VPCs on same node group have queued requests. Prioritize isolation: we should also spin up a small dedicated warm node for hanover if possible.
priya: @jamie go ahead with the policy change, but hold on the auto-scaling until we confirm node spin-up. I'll coordinate node add with infra.
jamie: applying policy now:```
PUT /v1/policies/temp-burst/hanover
{ "type":"qps-override", "target":"hanover-prod-1", "qps": 3.0, "duration":"6h", "revert": true }
```
jamie: policy accepted, reported id temp-burst-3123456789.
ops-bot: action log: policy temp-burst-3123456789 applied by jamie at 2026-03-15T12:07:12Z.
alex: monitoring metrics — 429 rate dropped to 2.3% within 30s. latency p50 stable. but tail p99 increased slightly for other tenants.
maria: contacting infra to spin up warm node now. @jamie can you add a routing weight to shift 20% of hanover traffic to fallback for long-context requests until new node is ready?
jamie: done. route rule added: if seq_len>2048 -> model=gptx-small-v2, weight=0.2.
account-anna: Hanover PM sent a note: they can temporarily slow batch jobs for 30m to reduce peak. They appreciate the quick response.
priya: create incident ticket and link to customer thread. alex can you take postmortem action items?
alex: will own postmortem. capturing action items now: 1) improve pre-emptive detection for context-length spikes; 2) add safe auto-scale path for dedicated pools; 3) update emergency override runbook to include capacity-check step.
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-3123456789, severity=sev2, assignees=[alex, jamie, priya].
alex: leaving a note for handoff — I'm oncall for next 40m, then @priya takes over. If anyone notices regression, page SRE again.
ops-bot: revert timer set for temp-burst-3123456789 at +6h (2026-03-15T18:07:12Z).
jamie: follow-up: spun an extra warm node in eu-west-1 (node-az2-warm-07) — capacity headroom improved. Monitoring shows stable 429 <1% across hanover pool.
maria: summary for CSM: emergency override applied, routing adjustments made, extra node provisioned. customer impact minimized, agreed temporary contract exception for 6h.
account-anna: will send formal confirmation and billing note to Hanover procurement.
priya: thanks team — keeping ticket open for postmortem and verifying auto-revert.
alex: closing thread for now, will update INC-2026-3123456789 once postmortem draft is ready. :white_check_mark:
